long_biography.plain_text:
Miami lawyer John Ruiz approached college athlete endorsements as a marketing business. When he arranged a prominent deal for basketball player Nijel Pack, he valued the attention surrounding a leading transfer prospect as well as the player's ability. His sponsorship programme also included less visible participants, such as long-snappers and athletes outside starting line-ups.

He wanted these commercial relationships to give students practical preparation for life after college. Alongside promotional work for his companies, he described helping athletes understand taxes and contractual obligations and introducing them to other potential business partners. He distinguished an athlete's advertising appeal from sporting performance alone.
